title: From Adam to the Flood
text: This period runs from the creation of Adam to the Flood of Noah’s day. Its length comes from adding the ages at which each father in the line from Adam to Noah had his son, and then Noah’s age when the Flood began. Ten generations are listed: Adam, Seth, Enosh, Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared, Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech and Noah.

pictures.title: God Made the First Man and Woman

title: From the Flood to the covenant with Abraham
text: The count continues through Noah’s son Shem and his descendants down to Terah, the father of Abraham. Abraham was 75 when he left Haran and crossed the Euphrates into Canaan, and the covenant Jehovah made with him took effect then, in 1943 B.C.E. The scattering from Babel happened within this period, in the days of Peleg, but the Bible gives no exact date for it.

pictures.title: Eight Survive Into a New World

title: From Abraham to the Exodus
text: The Bible gives this period directly as 430 years, to the very day. It falls into two halves of 215 years: first Abraham, Isaac and Jacob living as foreigners in Canaan, then, from Jacob’s move to Egypt in 1728 B.C.E., the years in Egypt that ended in slavery. It closes with the Passover and Israel’s deliverance in 1513 B.C.E.

pictures.title: The Miracle at the Red Sea

title: Forty years in the wilderness
text: Israel received the Law at Sinai and became a nation in a covenant with Jehovah. Because the people refused to enter the Promised Land, they wandered for forty years until that generation died out. Under Joshua they crossed the Jordan into Canaan in 1473 B.C.E.

title: The conquest and the Judges
text: From the entry into Canaan to Israel’s first king. The Bible does not give one total for these years. The figure is worked out from the periods on either side of it. The terms of the individual judges overlapped, because different judges served in different parts of the land at the same time.

pictures.title: A New Leader and Two Brave Women

title: The united kingdom
text: Saul, David and Solomon each ruled about forty years over all twelve tribes. Solomon began building the temple in his fourth year, 1034 B.C.E., which the Bible places in the 480th year after the Exodus. When Solomon died in 997 B.C.E. the kingdom split in two.

title: The two kingdoms
text: Judah in the south kept David’s line and Jerusalem. Israel in the north had its own kings until Assyria took Samaria in 740 B.C.E. Comparing the reigns in the books of Kings gives 390 years from the division to the destruction of Jerusalem, and Ezekiel’s prophecy points to the same number.

title: Seventy years of desolation
text: After Jerusalem was destroyed, the land of Judah lay empty and the people were exiles in Babylon. This period is dated by counting back from a fixed point in history: Babylon fell to Cyrus in 539 B.C.E., and the Jews he released were back in their cities by the autumn of 537. Seventy years before that is 607 B.C.E.

title: Return and rebuilding
text: The returned exiles laid the temple foundation in 536 B.C.E. and finished the building in 515. In 455 B.C.E., the twentieth year of Artaxerxes, Nehemiah was given permission to rebuild Jerusalem. That decree starts the count of Daniel’s seventy weeks of years leading to the Messiah. The last books of the Hebrew Scriptures were written in these years.

title: Under Persia, Greece and Rome
text: No Bible books were written in these centuries. The dates shown here follow the land of Judah as rule over it passed from Persia to Greece and then to Rome. Through all of it the count of Daniel’s seventy weeks, which began in 455 B.C.E., was running toward the Messiah’s arrival.
sources: si Study 3 ¶18, 19; the dates on this timeline

pictures.title: A Kingdom That Will Last Forever

title: The life of Jesus
text: Jesus was born about the autumn of 2 B.C.E. He was baptized in the autumn of 29 C.E., in the fifteenth year of Tiberius, when he was about thirty. That is 483 years, or 69 weeks of years, after the decree of 455 B.C.E. He died on Nisan 14 of 33 C.E., in the middle of the seventieth week.

pictures.title: Angels Announce the Birth of Jesus

title: The first-century congregation
text: The seventy weeks ended in 36 C.E., when Cornelius became the first uncircumcised Gentile Christian. The years that follow are dated from Paul’s journeys and from fixed points in Roman history. The Christian Greek Scriptures were written in this period. John wrote Revelation about 96 C.E. and his Gospel and letters about 98 C.E., which completed the Bible. He died about 100 C.E.

title: After the Bible was completed
text: The dates after 100 C.E. are not Bible events. They mark points in how the Bible was opposed, copied, translated and preserved, including how God’s name was rendered in English translations.
